case.title: A boy with a large head and autism
case.brief:
Referral from community paediatrics. A boy of 4 has a head circumference of +4.1 SD, global developmental delay and autism. His height is average. He has pigmented macules on the glans penis. His parents are well and their head circumferences are normal.

PTEN testing found a heterozygous variant, NM_000314.8:c.80-1G>C, at an intron 1 splice acceptor. Neither parent carries it; parentage has not been tested.
tasks: Work through the PVS1 decision tree for a canonical splice site. What does SpliceAI predict, and does it matter here?
The variant is absent from both parents, but parentage is unconfirmed: PS2 or PM6? How many points, given his phenotype?
Classify, sign and compare with the ClinGen PTEN expert panel.
What surveillance does a diagnosis of PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome bring, for him and later in life?
case.source: Variant: NM_000314.8(PTEN):c.80-1G>C, GRCh38 10-87894024-G-C, ClinGen allele CA000586 (absent from gnomAD v4.1). ClinVar VCV000189462; ClinGen PTEN VCEP classification (Evidence Repository). Checked October 2026. The patient and family are fictional.

patients.ref: Case 8: boy with a large head, developmental delay and autism
patients.referral: Community paediatrics: head circumference +4.1 SD, global developmental delay and a diagnosis of autism.
patients.summary: Boy of 4. Head circumference +4.1 SD (it crossed centiles upwards in the first year); height on the 50th centile. Global developmental delay (walked at 22 months, few words) and autism. Pigmented macules on the glans penis. No seizures.
patients.familyHistory: Parents unrelated, well, with normal head circumferences. Neither parent carries the variant; parentage has not been tested.
patients.notes: Fictional patient and family; the variant and the published evidence about it are real.

expected.source: ClinGen PTEN expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository, specifications v3.1.0; ClinVar VCV000189462 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2025-12-05).

notes.PVS1: A canonical splice acceptor (−1) of PTEN, where loss of function causes disease: full strength by the decision tree.
notes.PM6: Strong, by the panel’s rule: one assumed de novo occurrence (parents tested, parentage not confirmed) counts as strong in a person with a highly specific phenotype, such as macrocephaly with developmental delay. This patient is such a case.
notes.PP3: Not met: SpliceAI gives only 0.33 for this change, and a canonical site variant is assessed under PVS1. A low SpliceAI score doesn’t undo PVS1 at a canonical site, with one exception in the ACGS 2024 guidelines: a +2T>C change, which can leave a working GC donor, needs SpliceAI of 0.8 or more. This variant is at an acceptor’s −1, so the exception does not apply.
notes.BP7: Not met: it is at the −1 position of an intron, not a synonymous or deep intronic change.
